note_on_method: Each venue page rests on two City of Las Vegas records: the park's own page, whose header gives the address, the postcode and the park hours and whose amenity list counts the courts in a parenthesis, and the City's pickleball post of 11 March 2026, which counts them in a sentence. The county and the postcode come from the US Census address geocoder. At three venues both records count and agree. At Lorenzi and Patriot only the post counts, and the venue page says so. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts in a neighbourhood park in the north-west of Las Vegas, counted twice by the City: "Pickleball courts (4)" in the amenity list and "Four at Aloha Shores Park" in its pickleball post of 11 March 2026.

The park's description is the only one among the five published parks that names the game: "This neighborhood park features pickleball courts." Around the courts the City lists bocce and horseshoe courts, tennis courts, volleyball courts, a playground, a walk/jog track, a reservable picnic area and a barbecue grill. It does not list restrooms, and that is recorded as unknown rather than as a no.
slots.getting_there: 7550 Sauer St, Las Vegas, NV 89128, in Clark County. The US Census address geocoder matched "7550 SAUER, LAS VEGAS, NV, 89128" at house-number level and placed it in the incorporated place Las Vegas city, which is what allows it to publish under Las Vegas rather than under the county. The City publishes nothing about parking here.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts is two games at once, or a group of eight rotating without a long wait. Park hours are 7 a.m. to 11 p.m., printed in the page header.

Nothing on the park page or the post mentions lighting at the pickleball courts, and an 11 p.m. closing is a fact about the park rather than the lamps, so lighting is recorded as unknown. No price is stated either way, and no surface. The City does not call these courts indoor or outdoor, and never says whether the four are dedicated or share ground with the tennis courts.

faqs.a: Four, stated twice by the City: "Pickleball courts (4)" in the park's amenity list and "Four at Aloha Shores Park" on its pickleball post of 11 March 2026.
Not stated. Neither the park page nor the post mentions lighting, and park hours of 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. are about the gate, not the lamps.
Not stated. The City publishes no price for these courts either way.

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts on the largest site published in Las Vegas, "a 120-acre state-of-the-art regional park" in the far north-west. The count is "Pickleball courts (2)" in the amenity list and "Two at Centennial Hills Park" on the City's post of 11 March 2026; the two records agree.

The City's description is about the park rather than the courts. It "features a playground with ramps and features for all abilities" and is "built around an historic inverted riverbed thought to be the last remaining remnant of a large network of such channels that once covered this area". The rest of the amenity list is long: a dog park, sand volleyball courts, soccer fields, water play areas, concession stands and an "Amphitheatre with grass seating for more than 3,000". Nothing says where the two courts sit inside 120 acres.

The US Census address geocoder matched "7101 N BUFFALO DR, LAS VEGAS, NV, 89131" at house-number level and placed it in the incorporated place Las Vegas city. The City's header writes it "7101 N. Buffalo Drive, 89131". The City publishes nothing about parking, and its amenity list does not mention restrooms, though it does list concession stands.
slots.what_to_expect:
Two courts is a game, not a rotation. Park hours are 7 a.m. to 11 p.m., in the page header.

Lighting is not stated, and this page does not read the 11 p.m. closing as a promise; daylight is the safe plan. No price is stated, no surface, and the City never calls the courts indoor or outdoor. There are no tennis courts in the amenity list, so the two pickleball courts are not sharing a tennis slab the page admits to.

faqs.a: Two, stated twice: "Pickleball courts (2)" in the amenity list and "Two at Centennial Hills Park" on the City's post. Two courts is a game rather than a rotation.
Not stated. Nothing on the park page or the post mentions lighting at the pickleball courts.
The City says nothing about either. Concession stands are listed; restrooms and parking are not.

slots.description:
Seven pickleball courts, the largest published set in Las Vegas, at a park in the north-west built around an 18-hole executive golf course. The count is the City's twice over: "Pickleball courts (7)" in the amenity list and "Seven at Durango Hills Park" on its post of 11 March 2026.

The description above the list is about the golf: "This park features the 18-hole executive golf course Durango Hills Golf Club." The amenity list beside the courts is short and athletic: basketball courts, a skate park, a walking/jogging track, a picnic area, a playground and open space. No tennis courts are listed, so the seven are not sharing a tennis slab the page admits to. There is no restroom line.
slots.getting_there: 3521 N Durango Dr, Las Vegas, NV 89129, Clark County. Durango Dr, 89129". The City publishes nothing about parking at this park, and its amenity list does not mention restrooms.
slots.what_to_expect:
Seven courts is a rotation, which makes this the one Las Vegas venue where turning up alone is a reasonable plan. Park hours are 7 a.m. to 11 p.m., printed in the page header.

Whether any of that is lit is not stated. Nothing on the park page or the post mentions lighting at the pickleball courts, so this page does not read the 11 p.m. closing as a promise. No price is stated and no surface, and the City never calls the courts indoor or outdoor.

faqs.a: Seven, stated twice: "Pickleball courts (7)" in the amenity list and "Seven at Durango Hills Park" on the City's post. It is the largest published count in Las Vegas.
The City does not explain it. Seven is an odd number for a pickleball layout, and this page prints the figure as the City states it rather than rounding it to a pairing.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts on the City's count, "Four at Lorenzi Park" in its pickleball post of 11 March 2026, at a park the City lists on its Historic Property Register as an historic district and on the Nevada State Register of Historic Places.

This venue rests on one City record and says so. The park's own page lists tennis courts "managed by No Quit Tennis Academy", basketball courts, a band shell, reservable soccer and softball fields, a spring-fed fishing pond and the Sammy Davis Jr. Festival Plaza, and it never mentions pickleball. The record that states a number publishes.

The park opened "as Lorenzi's Lake Park in 1926 with a pool, dance pavilion, lakes and orchards" on 80 acres bought by David G. Lorenzi in 1912. In 1940 it became Twin Lakes Lodge, a 48-room hotel.

3333 W Washington Ave, Las Vegas, NV 89107, Clark County. The US Census address geocoder matched "3333 W WASHINGTON AVE, LAS VEGAS, NV, 89107" at house-number level and placed it in the incorporated place Las Vegas city. The City's header writes it "3333 W. Washington Ave., 89107".

The City publishes nothing about parking and its amenity list does not mention restrooms. Where the four courts sit relative to the twin lakes or the tennis academy's courts is not stated.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts is two games at once, if they are where the City's post says they are. That is the honest caveat here: the count comes from a blog post and not from the page that describes the park, and a reader who arrives with the park page in hand will find no mention of pickleball on it.

Park hours are 7 a.m. to 11 p.m., in the page header. Lighting is not stated for the pickleball courts, so daylight is the plan. No price is stated and no surface.

faqs.a: Four, on the City's pickleball post of 11 March 2026: "Four at Lorenzi Park". The park's own page never mentions pickleball, so this venue rests on one record.

faqs.q: Why does the park page not mention pickleball?
faqs.a: The City does not say. Its post counts four courts here and its park page lists tennis, basketball, a band shell and a fishing pond without them.
Not stated. Nothing on either City record mentions lighting at the pickleball courts.

slots.description:
Two pickleball courts on the City's count, "Two at Patriot Park" in its pickleball post of 11 March 2026, at a neighbourhood park in the north-west of the city whose own page is one sentence long.

That sentence is: "This park features a basketball court, tennis courts, playground and picnic areas." There is no amenity list, no history and no pickleball. So this venue rests on one City record and says so: the post counts two courts here and the park page does not mention them. Patriot is the second of two Las Vegas venues in that position, with Lorenzi Park.

The name is the other small disagreement between the two records. The park page header reads "Patriot Community Park" and the post shortens it to "Patriot Park"; the page's name is the one published.
slots.getting_there: 4050 Thom Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89130, Clark County. The US Census address geocoder matched "4050 THOM BLVD, LAS VEGAS, NV, 89130" at house-number level and placed it in the incorporated place Las Vegas city. The City's header writes it "4050 Thom Blvd., 89130". It publishes nothing about parking and nothing about restrooms; with no amenity list on the page there is not even a silence to read.
slots.what_to_expect:
Two courts is a game, not a rotation, and this is the venue in Las Vegas where the least is known about what you will find. If the two courts are lined onto the tennis courts, the City does not say so; if they stand alone, it does not say that either.

Park hours are 7 a.m. to 11 p.m., printed in the header. Lighting is not stated, and daylight is the plan. No price is stated, no surface, and the City never calls the courts indoor or outdoor.

faqs.a: Two, on the City's pickleball post of 11 March 2026: "Two at Patriot Park". The park's own page does not mention pickleball, so this venue rests on one record.

faqs.q: Why is it called Patriot Community Park here?
faqs.a: Because that is the name in the park page header. The City's post shortens it to "Patriot Park".

faqs.q: What else is in the park?
faqs.a: In the City's one sentence: "a basketball court, tennis courts, playground and picnic areas". There is no amenity list and no restroom or parking line.
